proofs.full_local_argument:
1. Put q=(p-1)/2>0. At a positive step write x=x_i, y=y_i, z=x_{i+1}, a=omega(y,x)>0, b=omega(z,y), lambda=(1/2)a^(-q), alpha=p!lambda/L_p. Exact prox optimality along the feasible segment from z to any u gives <alpha F(y)+grad d(z)-grad d(x),u-z>>=0. Expanding omega gives alpha<F(y),z-u> <= omega(u,x)-omega(u,z)-omega(z,x). This uses differentiability and convex feasibility directly.

2. The exact subproblem inequality with test point z gives <T_{p-1}(y;x),y-z> <= (2L_p/p!)a^q<grad d(x)-grad d(y),y-z>. Multiplication by alpha makes the coefficient 2lambda a^q=1. Expanding omega therefore gives alpha<T_{p-1}(y;x),y-z> <= omega(z,x)-omega(z,y)-omega(y,x). Adding to step 1 yields alpha<F(y),y-u> <= omega(u,x)-omega(u,z)-a-b+alpha<F(y)-T_{p-1}(y;x),y-z>.

3. Duality and the Taylor remainder bound give alpha<F(y)-T,y-z> <= lambda ||y-x||^p ||y-z|| <= (1/2)a^(-q)*a^(p/2)*b^(1/2)=(1/2)sqrt(ab). The inequality (sqrt(a)/4-sqrt(b))^2>=0 implies (1/2)sqrt(ab)<=a/16+b. Consequently alpha_i<F(y_i),y_i-u> <= omega(u,x_i)-omega(u,x_{i+1})-(15/16)a_i. Sum i=0,...,N-1 and use omega(u,x_N)>=0 to obtain (p!/L_p)sum_i lambda_i<F(y_i),y_i-u> <= omega(u,x_0)-(15/16)sum_i a_i. This holds for every u in X and every N>=1, including K=0; the printed Lemma's K>=1 restriction is not needed for this derivation.

4. Let S=sum_i lambda_i>0 and v=sum_i lambda_i y_i/S in X. Direct expansion gives A:=sum_i lambda_i<F(y_i),y_i-v> = (1/(2S))sum_{i,j}lambda_i lambda_j<F(y_i)-F(y_j),y_i-y_j>. Every summand is nonnegative by monotonicity, so A>=0. Substitute u=v in step 3. This substitution is legitimate because that inequality holds for every comparator after fixing the trajectory. It gives (15/16)sum_i a_i <= omega(v,x_0)-(p!/L_p)A <= Omega. Hence sum_i a_i<=16Omega/15. No arbitrary-comparator sign claim, solution comparator, solution existence or additional radius is required.

5. For Omega>0 put R=16Omega/15. On t>0, f(t)=t^(-q) has f''(t)=q(q+1)t^(-q-2)>0 and is decreasing. For m=(sum_i a_i)/N>0, the tangent inequality f(a_i)>=f(m)+f'(m)(a_i-m) gives sum_i f(a_i)>=Nf(m)>=N(R/N)^(-q). Thus S=(1/2)sum_i a_i^(-q)>=(1/2)N^(q+1)/R^q. This establishes the power-sum estimate without relying on an unreviewed external scientific dependency.

6. For any u in X, monotonicity implies <F(u),v-u>=(1/S)sum_i lambda_i<F(u),y_i-u> <= (1/S)sum_i lambda_i<F(y_i),y_i-u>. Step 3, dropping its nonpositive step term, bounds this by L_p omega(u,x_0)/(p!S). Step 5 therefore gives (2L_p/p!)*(16Omega/15)^q*omega(u,x_0)/N^(q+1). Since omega(u,x_0)<=Omega, the simultaneous uniform bound is (2L_p/p!)*(16/15)^q*Omega^(q+1)/N^(q+1), exactly the baseline conclusion.

7. Set r=(p+1)/2 and C=(2L_p/p!)*(16/15)^q. For known B>=Omega>0, T=(16/15)*(2L_p/(p!epsilon))^(1/r)*B dominates (C*B^r/epsilon)^(1/r), because 16/15>=(16/15)^(q/r). Therefore the single integer N_epsilon=max{1,ceil(T)} ensures C*Omega^r/N_epsilon^r<=epsilon simultaneously for all u. Indices i=0,...,N_epsilon-1 mean exactly N_epsilon subproblem calls on a nonterminal run.

8. Local terminal completion, separate from the source text and pinned Algorithm: if a_i=0, omega(y_i,x_i)>=||y_i-x_i||^2 forces y_i=x_i. Then T_{p-1}(x_i;x_i)=F(x_i), and the regularization term is zero since q>0. Thus U_{p,x_i}(y_i)=F(y_i), and the exact subproblem gives <F(y_i),y_i-u><=0 for all u. Monotonicity gives <F(u),y_i-u><=<F(y_i),y_i-u><=0. Taking u=y_i shows that the supremum is exactly 0. Return y_i before forming the negative power of zero. This uses at most the planned subproblem calls. If Omega=0, the Bregman lower bound forces X={x_0}; x_0 has zero gap without calls.

9. Every positive-step update and weighted output coincide with the baseline and published exact nonzero-step Algorithm. The proof uses only baseline monotonicity, Taylor remainder, Bregman normalization, finite Omega and exact interfaces, without strengthening those assumptions. Source p=1 and the stronger printed pointwise formula remain outside this claim. Each positive step separately charges one exact regularized VI solve, F(y_i), one exact prox and Taylor model construction. No efficient implementation, approximate-solve transfer or unrestricted Oracle Complexity conclusion follows.

assumptions: For all u,v in X, ||F(u)-T_{p-1}(u;v)||_* <= (L_p/p!)||u-v||^p, using the same norm as the Bregman lower bound.

The Definition 3.1 strong-VI Oracle returns an exact solution for each requested center, and each displayed prox minimization is solved exactly. These are interface assumptions, not implementation or uniqueness claims.

Finite Omega and N positive-step iterations are already conditions of the assigned baseline. A separately identified local terminal completion covers a zero step; it does not modify the published Algorithm record.
statement.conclusion: For N positive steps, sup_{u in X}<F(u),xhat-u> <= (2L_p/p!)*(16/15)^((p-1)/2)*Omega^((p+1)/2)/N^((p+1)/2). The more precise pointwise bound proved here is (2L_p/p!)*(16Omega/15)^((p-1)/2)*omega(u,x_0)/N^((p+1)/2). Thus N_epsilon suffices for uniform weak gap <=epsilon. A local zero-step terminal output has weak gap exactly 0. The stronger printed pointwise formula involving only omega(u,x_0)^((p+1)/2) is not asserted.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let X be a nonempty closed convex subset of R^n, n>=1, x_0 in X, and fix a norm with dual norm. Let d be differentiable on X and omega(u,v)=d(u)-d(v)-<grad d(v),u-v> >= ||u-v||^2 for all u,v in X. Define Omega=sup_{u in X}omega(u,x_0)<infinity. Let F:X->R^n be continuous and monotone, with derivatives defining T_{p-1}(u;v)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}D^jF(v)[u-v]^j/j!. Put q=(p-1)/2. Initialize x_0. For i=0,...,N-1 query an exact y_i in X satisfying <U_{p,x_i}(y_i),y_i-u><=0 for every u in X, where U_{p,v}(u)=T_{p-1}(u;v)+(2L_p/p!)omega(u,v)^q(grad d(u)-grad d(v)). For a_i=omega(y_i,x_i)>0 set lambda_i=(1/2)a_i^(-q), alpha_i=p!lambda_i/L_p, and x_{i+1}=argmin_{u in X}{alpha_i<F(y_i),u-y_i>+omega(u,x_i)}. Return xhat=sum_i lambda_i y_i/S, where S=sum_i lambda_i.
statement.parameter_domains: Integer p>=2, L_p>0, integer N=K+1>=1, epsilon>0, finite Omega>=0. This preserves the baseline parameter scope. If Omega=0, X={x_0} and x_0 is returned without calls. For Omega>0 the printed weighted output requires positive a_i at each executed step. Optional local terminal completion: test a_i=0 immediately after the subproblem call and return y_i before forming lambda_i; otherwise continue the printed update.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such instance, every N>=1 and every sequence of exact interface choices with N positive steps, the same output satisfies the bound simultaneously for all u in X. No VI solution-existence assumption or solution-dependent radius is used. Given a known B>=Omega>0, choose the single integer N_epsilon=max{1,ceil((16/15)*(2L_p/(p!epsilon))^(2/(p+1))*B)} in advance. This uniformly suffices for all comparators. With the local zero-step completion it suffices for every run using at most N_epsilon subproblem calls. The bound is pathwise; deterministic interface selection gives a deterministic Algorithm.
